subject.title: fix(openshell): mirror sandboxes can modify workspace skill files despite read-only policy

question: Should OpenShell mirror sandboxes with `workspaceAccess: "rw"` be brought into parity with Docker and remote sandbox skill-root immutability, accepting that intentionally editing workspace skill directories from a sandbox will now fail?
rationale: The implementation is narrowly aligned with the existing sibling policy, but changing a writable sandbox’s reachable filesystem contract is a security-boundary and compatibility decision that requires owner intent.

options.title: Approve protected-root parity
options.body: Accept the documented behavior change and merge after rebasing and confirming the focused OpenShell tests still pass.

options.title: Keep OpenShell behavior distinct
options.body: Do not merge if writable workspace skill directories are an intentional OpenShell contract that needs a separately documented product decision.

recommendation.title: Approve protected-root parity
recommendation.body: Accept the documented behavior change and merge after rebasing and confirming the focused OpenShell tests still pass.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged sandbox-skill work is the strongest available ownership signal for the cross-backend policy this PR extends.
